'''Greg Anderson''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Rogue 31 from Ellicott City, Md. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run. At DecipherCon 1999 Greg also played [[Young Jedi]]: finished 9 in YJ Opposites.<ref name="dc99yj20_5">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ20_5.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: YJ Opposites], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010108191900/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ20_5.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Squadron listing ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Slot !! Town !! Status (fan table)

| Rogue 31 || Ellicott City, Md || Retired

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Other sourced notes ==

Rogue 31, Ellicott City, Maryland. Named in Holland's 25 January 2002 announcement as a first Player Advocate for Rules Support (with Joe Helfrich).

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Anderson playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref>
